To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the gameful design elements that are preferred by the most users in our study are those that are associated to a sense of accomplishment, and that the users most likely to enjoy gameful design elements are those who are young males, who are high on extraversion, and who are high on conscientiousness.
the most important design elements are: 1. Challenge, 2. Social Interaction, and 3. Progression.

1) the eight design element groups are: "challenge", "competition", "socialization", "storytelling", "immersive environment", "reward", "feedback", and "progress"; 2) "competition", "challenge", and "progress" are the design elements that most participants prefer; 3) participants who are more likely than the average to prefer "storytelling" and "progress" tend to be older, more extroverted, and more conscientious;
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question: "Which design elements should we apply to which users?".
understanding how users' characteristics influence the effectiveness of gameful design.
understanding user preferences in gameful design.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the design elements of the group "Social Interaction" are most preferred by all types of gamification users, while the design elements of group "Gameplay" are most preferred among the users who are already familiar with digital games.

the most important design elements are those that make the user feel that he/she has achieved something, that the user feels that he/she is progressing towards a goal, and that the user is being rewarded for his/her actions.
the design of gameful applications requires a deep understanding of the users' preferences and their characteristics.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have found that there is no one-size-fits-all design for gameful systems, but rather that different types of people prefer different types of gameful design.
gameful design should not be a matter of adding elements to a system but rather a matter of adding the right elements to the right users.
the most important game elements are those which provide a clear and meaningful goal, which are easy to learn and which provide a sense of progression.
The main takeaway from our work is that
gameful design is not a single design strategy.
the gameful design space is more nuanced than previously thought.
we can design gameful systems to appeal to a broad spectrum of users by using a variety of design elements.
